opening: You remember that moment. Your Tokyo teammate refreshes their browser and sees your app materialize, teleported exactly as you built it. Preview Domains make this possible. Those cryptic URLs look like a cat walked across a keyboard. But then the page loads and immediately starts hunting for a database at "localhost:3000." The teleportation succeeded, but your code has an identity crisis. It doesn't know it's in Tokyo. It thinks it's still on your laptop. Your application acts like a theater act
keyPoints: How **Environment Variables** act as chameleon-like configuration that shifts based on **Deployment Context**
Why **Scope** (Production vs Preview) creates safe boundaries between live systems and experiments
The distinction between public configuration variables and encrypted **Secrets**, and how encryption at rest protects the latter
How **domain type** (custom domains for Production, generated URLs for Preview) signals the platform which variable set to inject
Why hardcoding configuration creates "identity crisis" failures when code teleports from laptop to server
